18:- **Android shell.** The application id is `dev.exedev.emailos.androidfixture` (`src-tauri/gen/android/app/build.gradle.kts`, `src-tauri/tauri.android.conf.json`). Track A's ADR 0004 proposes renaming it to `dev.exedev.emailos`, pending owner approval. It also moves the Kotlin sources out of `.../androidfixture/` and turns backups off. The manifest asks only for `INTERNET` (`src-tauri/gen/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`). `MainActivity.kt` handles insets and Back. The shell uses no Tauri plugins. The `main-window` capability says "No plugins, no shell, no broad capability grants" (`src-tauri/capabilities/main-window.json`).
19:- **Emulator.** `emulator-5554` runs a Google Play image (`sdk_gphone64_x86_64`). It has the Play Store (`com.android.vending`) and Google Play services (`com.google.android.gms`) version 24.23.35, which is from about June 2024. These facts were checked by the coordinator on the running device. The `t3-pixel` AVD config on disk says `google_apis`; the running device is what counts. See the Play services risk below.
50:- **Keystore-encrypted file behind `Secrets`** (AES-256-GCM key generated in Android Keystore, not exportable; ciphertext in the app's `no_backup` directory; encrypt and decrypt in Kotlin, called from Rust through the bridge). *(Recommended)*
88:- **Backup and reinstall.** Track A (ADR 0004) sets `android:allowBackup="false"` with exclusion rules. B relies on that and does not change backup settings itself. B adds one test: the binding file lives in `noBackupFilesDir`, so it stays out of any backup even if A's rules change later. Keystore keys are never backed up, so a restored ciphertext could not be decrypted anyway. An uninstall deletes app data and the Keystore key. A reinstall starts at the first-run screen and needs **Connect Gmail** again. Google still remembers the grant, so the consent screen may be skipped; the account chooser can still appear.
164:- Signing keys, the package name, backup settings, release builds, first-launch ANR and physical-device install (track A).
182:| **External, Testing** | "Authorizations by a test user will expire seven days from the time of consent". The only exception is apps that request nothing beyond name, email and profile, so Gmail scopes get the 7-day rule. At most 100 test users ([Manage app audience](https://support.google.com/cloud/answer/15549945); [OAuth 2.0: refresh token expiration](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2#expiration)). | **Sign-in expired** every week; **Sign in again** shows the consent screen again. Usable for a validation run, not for daily use. |
183:| **External, In production, not verified** | The app "might display an 'unverified app' screen before it displays the consent screen" ([Unverified apps](https://support.google.com/cloud/answer/7454865)). It is limited to "100 new users in total", over the project's lifetime ([Manage app audience](https://support.google.com/cloud/answer/15549945)). The restricted-scope verification page names personal use as a case where verification may not be needed: "if you are the only user of your app or if your app is used by only a few users, all of whom are known personally to you" ([Restricted scope verification](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2/production-readiness/restricted-scope-verification)). Google states the 7-day expiry **only** for Testing. It does **not** say whether authorizations last longer for an unverified production app with restricted scopes. The general expiry rules (six months unused; password change for Gmail scopes) still apply. | The owner clicks through the unverified-app screen at each consent. That expected screen is the only ongoing cost. **Unconfirmed:** whether consent survives past 7 days. To check, at least 8 days after consent, kill and relaunch the app; it must sync with no sign-in UI (validation plan). |
186:**Recommendation:** **Personal mode**, in a new project created by the Google account the owner will read on the phone. If it does not accept the Gmail scopes, or is not offered for that account, use **External, In production, not verified**. Keep the "unverified app" screen at consent, and confirm the 8-day check before relying on it. **Testing** is only for a throwaway validation account. Because a Personal project accepts only its creator, a throwaway emulator account needs its own small project: either its own Personal project created while signed in as that account, or an External Testing project where it is a test user.
194:   - For a throwaway validation project, keep **Testing** and add the throwaway account as a **Test user**.
197:   - Package name: the final application id from track A. ADR 0004 proposes `dev.exedev.emailos`. Register the id that is merged, not today's `dev.exedev.emailos.androidfixture`.
209:  - the moved Kotlin package path (`MainActivity.kt` out of `.../androidfixture/`);
210:  - `allowBackup="false"` with exclusion rules.
212:  B does **not** repeat or change the backup settings. B adds to A's files only:
301:- **Consent lifetime.** Testing expires every 7 days (documented). Personal mode documents no 7-day expiry, but its pages do not say explicitly that restricted Gmail scopes are allowed. Unverified production has no documented 7-day rule but no positive statement either. The 8-day check in the validation plan settles it for the chosen setup.
310:4. *(Resolved by the coordinator: backup settings are track A's, ADR 0004.)*
12:- **OAuth is the desktop loopback flow.** `crates/mail-core/src/gmail/auth.rs:192` `authorize` makes a PKCE verifier, challenge and state (`auth.rs:177`). It binds `127.0.0.1:0` and opens the URL with the `webbrowser` crate (`auth.rs:144`). It then waits up to `AUTH_TIMEOUT` = 180 s for the exact callback path and state (`auth.rs:239`). `exchange_code` (`auth.rs:382`) and `refresh` (`auth.rs:404`) talk to the token endpoint. The client id comes from `EMAIL_OS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` in the launch environment (`GoogleConfig::from_env`, `auth.rs:70`). If it is missing, the app reports a visible `not_configured`. A phone has no launch environment.
77:- **When UI is needed:** with `interactive = true`, the bridge launches the `PendingIntent` from `MainActivity` and resolves when the activity result arrives. Back or dismissing the sheet resolves `cancelled`, which maps to `AuthCancelled`. The existing 180 s `AUTH_TIMEOUT` and `CancelToken` still bound the wait on the Rust side. Silent calls (`interactive = false`) never show UI. If UI would be needed, they return `needsUserInteraction`, which maps to `AuthRequired` (**Sign-in expired** → **Sign in again**).

+**Status:** Proposed (revised after coordinator review) — track B of the "usable Android app" programme. Nothing here is implemented. Implementation starts only after the coordinator's GREENLIGHT.
## Context

- `AndroidKeystoreSecrets` implements `Secrets`. It stores the serialized `TokenBundle` encrypted with an AES-256-GCM Keystore key (alias `email-os-gmail-binding`, no user authentication required, so sync can run while the app is open and unlocked). The file is in `noBackupFilesDir`. Under option C the bundle holds **no token material**: only the account id, the address and the granted scopes (section 4). The token fields stay in the type for desktop. On Android they are always empty, and a test asserts the stored JSON has no token.

- **No plaintext fallback.** A missing key, a failed decryption, a corrupt file or a Keystore error all return `SecretsUnavailable`, shown as today. **Disconnect** (`clear`) deletes the file and the key; it is the documented way to recover from a broken store. The fixture never touches it.

-- **Backup and reinstall.** Track A (ADR 0004) sets `android:allowBackup="false"` with exclusion rules. B relies on that and does not change backup settings itself. B adds one test: the binding file lives in `noBackupFilesDir`, so it stays out of any backup even if A's rules change later. Keystore keys are never backed up, so a restored ciphertext could not be decrypted anyway. An uninstall deletes app data and the Keystore key. A reinstall starts at the first-run screen and needs **Connect Gmail** again. Google still remembers the grant, so the consent screen may be skipped; the account chooser can still appear.

content.text:
ADR READY: docs/adr/0005-android-gmail-sign-in.md @ b81c6e8ab00227b8a6e97838cb8a1dde96632b9a

All six review points are in. The first push failed and the retry went through; nothing is implemented.

1. **Emulator:** the ADR now uses your facts: a Google Play image with Play Store and Play services 24.23.35. Google documents no minimum Play services version for `authorize()`. Because it is older than the library releases that added `clearToken` and `revokeAccess` (July 2025), it very likely works on 24.23.35. That is my inference, not documented, so the emulator can probably run the real flow with a throwaway account.
   - `clearToken` and `revokeAccess` may be missing from a June 2024 Play services. If so, the bridge reports them as unsupported and the app copes: it drops its own copy of the token and asks again silently, and disconnect stays local.
   - The first step of stage 3 is a temporary test on the emulator that records which of the three calls work.
   - With a Google account signed in, the Play Store could update Play services. That would change the shared emulator, so I would only do it with your agreement.
2. **Weekly expiry:** the ADR now compares three publishing setups, quoting Google's pages:
   - **Testing:** sign-in expires 7 days after consent, and Gmail scopes are not exempt. Weekly re-consent.
   - **In production, not verified:** Google shows an "unverified app" screen and caps the app at 100 new users over its lifetime. Google states the 7-day expiry only for Testing and says nothing either way about this setup.
   - **Personal mode:** a project type you pick when creating a new project. Google says it needs no verification, has no user cap, no 7-day expiry and no unverified-app screen. Only the account that created it can sign in, and an existing project cannot switch to it. Its pages do not say explicitly whether restricted Gmail scopes are allowed.

   **Recommendation:** Personal mode, created by the account the phone will read. If it doesn't accept the Gmail scopes, use In production without verification. Use Testing only for the throwaway emulator account. A new check in the validation plan settles the gap: 8 or more days after first consent, kill and relaunch the app; it must sync with no sign-in screen.
3. **Track A:** A lands first. B's Android stages build on A's merged package name, Kotlin path and backup settings. B adds only the Play services dependency, activity-result forwarding in `MainActivity.kt`, and one new Kotlin file. My own backup-off item and owner question 4 are gone. Stages 1–2 are Rust-only and don't wait for A.
4. **Links:** `open_external_link` stays closed in B. Track C may reuse the bridge pattern or build its own.
5. **Track D:** each grant has a list of stored scopes that already cover it. If they do, `request_grant` returns `AlreadyCovered` without calling the sign-in service: no consent screen, no network. `grant_covered()` answers the same question for D's checks and UI. Tests assert zero sign-in calls in that case. D's `Send` is covered by `gmail.send` or `gmail.modify`.
6. **Open draft during a mode switch:** the switch works like Connect and Disconnect today (`src/App.vue:1359-1377`).
   - The frontend saves and closes the editor first and only then sends `switch_mode`.
   - If the save fails, the switch is not sent and the editor stays open with its error.
   - On the backend, `switch_mode` advances the draft service's session counter before stopping the old core. A save that arrives late is rejected and never written into the other profile.
   - There are tests for this in stages 4 and 5, plus an emulator check.

**Owner questions to pass on** (4 and 5 are marked resolved in the ADR; the numbers are unchanged):
1. Is depending on Google Play services acceptable, and does your phone have it?
2. First run: a choice screen (recommended), or open the demo by default?
3. Should Disconnect only clear the account on the phone (recommended), or also remove the app's access at Google?
6. Which throwaway Google account for the emulator, and will you sign it in yourself through the Device panel?
7. Google Cloud setup: a new Personal mode project (recommended), or a project published In production without verification? Personal mode cannot reuse the existing desktop project.

14:- **Token custody.** The `Secrets` trait (`secrets.rs:54-61`) has one production implementation, `KeychainSecrets`, which uses the macOS Keychain. On every other platform, Android included, it returns `SecretsUnavailable` (`secrets.rs:119-132`). There is no plaintext fallback, by design. `LiveGmailProvider::access_token` (`provider.rs:221`) loads the bundle and refreshes it with the stored refresh token (`provider.rs:262`). Credential publication is fenced so a disconnect or account change during OAuth cannot be overwritten (`provider.rs:76-92`, `provider/api.rs:110-130`).
15:- **Disconnect** clears the secret (`provider/api.rs:314-324`) and the core clears the Gmail cache. Drafts stay on the device. Google's grant is not revoked (`docs/development.md`, "Google Desktop OAuth setup").
18:- **Android shell.** The application id is `dev.exedev.emailos.androidfixture` (`src-tauri/gen/android/app/build.gradle.kts`, `src-tauri/tauri.android.conf.json`). Track A's ADR 0004 proposes renaming it to `dev.exedev.emailos`, pending owner approval. It also moves the Kotlin sources out of `.../androidfixture/` and turns backups off. The manifest asks only for `INTERNET` (`src-tauri/gen/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`). `MainActivity.kt` handles insets and Back. The shell uses no Tauri plugins. The `main-window` capability says "No plugins, no shell, no broad capability grants" (`src-tauri/capabilities/main-window.json`).
41:- Against: Google turned custom URI schemes **off by default** for Android clients in 2023. It must be switched on under the client's Advanced settings. Google says it may be removed later and recommends Google Identity Services instead ([Google Developers Blog](https://developers.googleblog.com/en/improving-user-safety-in-oauth-flows-through-new-oauth-custom-uri-scheme-restrictions/)). Any app can register the same scheme; PKCE protects the code, but the consent screen can still be impersonated. A long-lived refresh token sits on the phone. A verified App Link (https redirect) is not available for Android-type clients and would need a domain we control. **Viable fallback; not recommended as the primary path.**
43:**C. Google Identity Services Authorization API (`AuthorizationClient`, Play services) with an Android OAuth client bound to package name + SHA-1.** *(Recommended)*
44:A small Kotlin bridge calls `Identity.getAuthorizationClient(context).authorize(AuthorizationRequest)` with the scopes we need. Consent is shown by Play services through a `PendingIntent` that the Activity launches. The result carries an access token and the list of granted scopes. Calling `authorize()` again with the same scopes returns a fresh token without UI while the grant stands. The app never receives a refresh token, and Google's guidance is "Don't store refresh tokens on the device". `revokeAccess()` and `clearToken()` exist. Incremental scopes mean calling `authorize()` again with more scopes ([Android Developers: Authorize access to Google user data](https://developer.android.com/identity/authorization)). Play services matches the package name and signing certificate to the registered Android client, so no client id is written into the build. `requestOfflineAccess` (server auth code plus a Web client) is **not** used: there is no backend.
52:- **Plain app-private file.** Rejected: plaintext violates the no-plaintext-fallback rule even inside the app sandbox.
64:- **OAuth client:** one **Android** client in the owner's Google Cloud project for each (package name, SHA-1) pair the app is signed with. The package name and the release/debug signing keys come from track A (ADR 0004). No Web client and no client secret. The custom URI scheme toggle stays **off**.
65:- **No client id in the build.** Play services matches package + signature. "Configured" therefore cannot be known before the first call. A `DEVELOPER_ERROR` result (package/SHA-1 not registered) maps to `not_configured`, with a next step that says this build is not registered. "Play services missing or too old" maps to `unsupported_platform` on connect. The account status says so plainly; it is not shown as an expired sign-in.
69:  - `revokeAccess(account, scopes)`.
72:  `clearToken` and `revokeAccess` are newer than `authorize` (library 21.4.0, July 2025; see Risks). If the device's Play services does not implement them, they fail with an `ApiException`, and the bridge reports `unsupported`:
81:  - `PlatformAuthorizerSource` sits over a small `PlatformAuthorizer` trait (`authorize`, `clear_token`, `revoke`). On Android its implementation is the bridge. In tests it is a scripted fake, so the whole Android path is tested on Linux.
87:- **No plaintext fallback.** A missing key, a failed decryption, a corrupt file or a Keystore error all return `SecretsUnavailable`, shown as today. **Disconnect** (`clear`) deletes the file and the key; it is the documented way to recover from a broken store. The fixture never touches it.
111:- **Moving between modes.** The compact **Account** page shows in demo mode a **Use your own mail** row (→ `switch_mode("gmail")`), and in Gmail mode a **Switch to demo mailbox** row (→ `switch_mode("fixture")`). Switching to the demo **does not disconnect**: credentials, cache and drafts of the Gmail profile stay, and switching back resumes them. **Disconnect** keeps its desktop meaning: it is local, clears the binding and the Gmail cache, and keeps drafts. On Android it also calls `clearToken`. It does **not** revoke the Google grant unless the owner chooses that (owner question 3). After disconnect the app stays in Gmail mode on **Not connected**, where **Switch to demo mailbox** is available.
168:- Phones without Play services (option B stays available as a later fallback).
197:   - Package name: the final application id from track A. ADR 0004 proposes `dev.exedev.emailos`. Register the id that is merged, not today's `dev.exedev.emailos.androidfixture`.
198:   - SHA-1 certificate fingerprint: from track A's signing key (`keytool -list -v -keystore <keystore> -alias <alias>`).
200:   Register **one client per signing key used**: the emulator debug key on this VM (I will post its SHA-1 fingerprint, which is public, when stage 7 starts) and the key of any APK installed on your phone. Leave **Advanced settings → custom URI scheme** off. No Web client, no secret. No client id has to be sent to me or put in the build.
209:  - the moved Kotlin package path (`MainActivity.kt` out of `.../androidfixture/`);
217:  B also needs the **signing keys**, whose SHA-1 fingerprints the owner registers, for debug (emulator), CI and phone builds. A package rename after registration means a new Android client. Stages 1 and 2 are Rust-only and do not wait for A. A's first-launch ANR fix matters too: B never runs a silent `authorize` on the main thread.
234:2. **Credential seam.** Extract `CredentialSource` from `LiveGmailProvider`: `access_token`, `authorize(scopes, account, interactive)`, `invalidate(token)`, `revoke`. `LoopbackPkceSource` wraps today's `auth.rs`, with identical behaviour. Add `PlatformAuthorizerSource` over the `PlatformAuthorizer` trait and a scripted fake covering granted, missing modify, cancelled, needs-interaction, developer error, Play services missing, wrong account, network, and 401 → one silent retry → `AuthRequired`. *Check:* all existing provider and auth tests pass untouched; the new fake-driven tests pass; `cargo clippy` is clean.
237:   - `clearToken` and `revokeAccess`, reporting `unsupported` when the device's Play services lacks them;
241:   Add the Rust `#[cfg(target_os = "android")]` `AndroidPlatformAuthorizer` and `AndroidKeystoreSecrets` over `run_mobile_plugin`, and the `play-services-auth` dependency. No mode change yet: Android still opens fixture. **First step of the stage:** a debug-only probe records, on the emulator, whether Play services 24.23.35 accepts `authorize`, `clearToken` and `revokeAccess`. Before an Android client is registered, `authorize` is expected to reach Google and fail with `DEVELOPER_ERROR`, not "API unavailable". The probe is removed before commit. *Check:*
270:- Emulator, with a debug APK whose SHA-1 is not yet registered:
273:  - **Switch to demo mailbox** and back keeps both profiles' files (`run-as` listing);
285:  - revoke access in the Google account settings → **Sign-in expired** → **Sign in again**;
286:  - **Disconnect** → **Not connected**, cache gone, drafts kept, Keystore file gone (`run-as` listing only; file contents are never printed).
295:- **Play services dependency.** Phones without Google Play services cannot connect. If that matters, option B (custom URI scheme) is the fallback. It relies on a setting Google has deprecated.
297:  - What Google documents: `authorize()` fails "if authorization is not available on the device (for example, internal error or Play Services not available)", and unsupported calls "fail with an ApiException" ([AuthorizationClient reference](https://developers.google.com/android/reference/com/google/android/gms/auth/api/identity/AuthorizationClient); [Play services release notes](https://developers.google.com/android/guides/releases)). `clearToken` and `revokeAccess` were added in play-services-auth **21.4.0 (July 2025)**. I found no documented minimum Play services APK version for any of these calls.
298:  - Inferred, not documented: `authorize()` predates the 21.x library releases, so 24.23.35 very likely supports it. Then the emulator can run the real flow with a throwaway Google account. `clearToken` and `revokeAccess` may be missing from a June 2024 Play services.
299:  - Handling: stage 3's probe records what the emulator supports. The bridge treats missing `clearToken`/`revokeAccess` as `unsupported` and degrades as described in section 1. With a throwaway account signed in, the Play Store can update Play services; an update changes the emulator, so it needs the coordinator's agreement. The owner's phone, with current Play services, is the final check either way.
305:**Open questions for the owner**
307:1. Is depending on **Google Play services** (option C) acceptable? Does your phone have it? If not, should B build option B instead, accepting the deprecated custom-scheme setting and a refresh token on the phone?
309:3. **Disconnect:** local only, as on desktop (recommended), or also revoke the app's access at Google from the phone?

**Status:** Proposed (revised with the owner's decisions of 2026-11-21) — track B of the "usable Android app" programme. Nothing here is implemented. Implementation starts only after the coordinator's GREENLIGHT.

## Decisions (owner, 2026-11-21)

1. **Google Play services is a requirement.** The owner's phone has it. Option C, the Authorization API, is approved. There is **no** custom-scheme fallback (option B) in this programme. A phone without Play services keeps the demo mailbox.
2. **First run shows a choice screen** (your own mail or the demo mailbox). It can be switched later from **Account**.
3. **Disconnect is local only**, as on desktop: it clears the binding, the cached token and the Gmail cache, and keeps drafts. The app does **not** revoke access at Google. B therefore does not use `revokeAccess` at all.
4. **App id is `dev.exedev.emailos`** (track A, ADR 0004, approved). Release builds are signed with the owner's release key, which is held by the owner and CI. Debug and local builds use the debug key. B plans **one Android OAuth client per signer** (section 1 and Owner actions):
   - the release SHA-1, supplied by the owner;
   - the debug SHA-1 of this machine's debug keystore, which signs the emulator builds.

**Still open** (the coordinator will ask the owner):
- which Google account is used on the emulator;
- the same Cloud project as desktop or a new one;
- the publishing setup: Personal mode, In production unverified, or Testing.

## Context

lines: **B. Android OAuth client + Custom Tab + custom URI scheme redirect, with PKCE in Rust.**

The app opens the authorization URL in a Custom Tab. Google redirects to `<applicationId>:/oauth2redirect` (the exact form is to be confirmed against Google's documentation when implemented). `MainActivity` receives the intent and passes the URL to Rust. Rust checks `state` and exchanges the code with the stored PKCE verifier. The refresh token is kept in Android Keystore-backed storage behind `Secrets`.

- For: reuses `generate_pkce`, `exchange_code`, `refresh` and the publication fences. Only the "wait for callback" step changes, from a listener to a channel fed by `onNewIntent`. Works without Google Play services. Only the client id is needed (Android clients have no secret). It is not confidential and can be set at build time through a Gradle property, a `BuildConfig` field and the plugin.

-- Against: Google turned custom URI schemes **off by default** for Android clients in 2023. It must be switched on under the client's Advanced settings. Google says it may be removed later and recommends Google Identity Services instead ([Google Developers Blog](https://developers.googleblog.com/en/improving-user-safety-in-oauth-flows-through-new-oauth-custom-uri-scheme-restrictions/)). Any app can register the same scheme; PKCE protects the code, but the consent screen can still be impersonated. A long-lived refresh token sits on the phone. A verified App Link (https redirect) is not available for Android-type clients and would need a domain we control. **Viable fallback; not recommended as the primary path.**

**C. Google Identity Services Authorization API (`AuthorizationClient`, Play services) with an Android OAuth client bound to package name + SHA-1.** *(Recommended)*

A small Kotlin bridge calls `Identity.getAuthorizationClient(context).authorize(AuthorizationRequest)` with the scopes we need. Consent is shown by Play services through a `PendingIntent` that the Activity launches. The result carries an access token and the list of granted scopes. Calling `authorize()` again with the same scopes returns a fresh token without UI while the grant stands. The app never receives a refresh token, and Google's guidance is "Don't store refresh tokens on the device". `revokeAccess()` and `clearToken()` exist. Incremental scopes mean calling `authorize()` again with more scopes ([Android Developers: Authorize access to Google user data](https://developer.android.com/identity/authorization)). Play services matches the package name and signing certificate to the registered Android client, so no client id is written into the build. `requestOfflineAccess` (server auth code plus a Web client) is **not** used: there is no backend.

content.content:
**Open questions for the owner**

1. Is depending on **Google Play services** (option C) acceptable? Does your phone have it? If not, should B build option B instead, accepting the deprecated custom-scheme setting and a refresh token on the phone?
2. **First run:** a choice screen (recommended), or open the demo by default with **Use your own mail** only in Account?
3. **Disconnect:** local only, as on desktop (recommended), or also revoke the app's access at Google from the phone?
4. *(Resolved by the coordinator: backup settings are track A's, ADR 0004.)*
5. *(Resolved by the coordinator: links in bodies are track C's; `open_external_link` stays closed in B.)*
6. Which **Google account** will be used on the emulator? A throwaway one is recommended, holding only synthetic mail. Will you sign it in yourself through the Device panel when stage 7 starts?
7. **Google Cloud project setup:** a new **Personal mode** project created by the account the phone will read (recommended; see Owner actions), or an External project published **In production** without verification? A Personal project cannot be the existing desktop project, because existing projects cannot switch to Personal. Desktop can keep its current project, or add a Desktop client in the new one later.
9:3. **Disconnect is local only**, as on desktop: it clears the binding, the cached token and the Gmail cache, and keeps drafts. The app does **not** revoke access at Google. B therefore does not use `revokeAccess` at all.
58:A small Kotlin bridge calls `Identity.getAuthorizationClient(context).authorize(AuthorizationRequest)` with the scopes we need. Consent is shown by Play services through a `PendingIntent` that the Activity launches. The result carries an access token and the list of granted scopes. Calling `authorize()` again with the same scopes returns a fresh token without UI while the grant stands. The app never receives a refresh token, and Google's guidance is "Don't store refresh tokens on the device". `revokeAccess()` and `clearToken()` exist. Incremental scopes mean calling `authorize()` again with more scopes ([Android Developers: Authorize access to Google user data](https://developer.android.com/identity/authorization)). Play services matches the package name and signing certificate to the registered Android client, so no client id is written into the build. `requestOfflineAccess` (server auth code plus a Web client) is **not** used: there is no backend.
96:  There is no `revokeAccess`, because disconnect is local only (Decision 3). `clearToken` is newer than `authorize` (library 21.4.0, July 2025; see Risks). If the device's Play services does not implement it, the call fails with an `ApiException` and the bridge reports `unsupported`. Rust then drops its in-memory token and calls `authorize` silently. If that call returns the same rejected token, the result is `AuthRequired`. A failed `clearToken` never blocks a disconnect.
131:- **Moving between modes.** The compact **Account** page shows in demo mode a **Use your own mail** row (→ `switch_mode("gmail")`), and in Gmail mode a **Switch to demo mailbox** row (→ `switch_mode("fixture")`). Switching to the demo **does not disconnect**: credentials, cache and drafts of the Gmail profile stay, and switching back resumes them. **Disconnect** keeps its desktop meaning: it is local, clears the binding and the Gmail cache, and keeps drafts. On Android it also calls `clearToken`. It does **not** revoke the Google grant (Decision 3); a user who wants that uses their Google account settings. After disconnect the app stays in Gmail mode on **Not connected**, where **Switch to demo mailbox** is available.
307:  - revoke access in the Google account settings → **Sign-in expired** → **Sign in again**;

I found no documented minimum Play services APK version for any of these calls.
321:  - Inferred, not documented: `authorize()` predates the 21.x library releases, so 24.23.35 very likely supports it. Then the emulator can run the real flow with a throwaway Google account. `clearToken` and `revokeAccess` may be missing from a June 2024 Play services.

204:| **External, In production, not verified** | The app "might display an 'unverified app' screen before it displays the consent screen" ([Unverified apps](https://support.google.com/cloud/answer/7454865)). It is limited to "100 new users in total", over the project's lifetime ([Manage app audience](https://support.google.com/cloud/answer/15549945)). The restricted-scope verification page names personal use as a case where verification may not be needed: "if you are the only user of your app or if your app is used by only a few users, all of whom are known personally to you" ([Restricted scope verification](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2/production-readiness/restricted-scope-verification)). +**Status:** Approved by the coordinator (2026-11-21), with the owner's decisions below — track B of the "usable Android app" programme. Nothing here is implemented. Implementation starts only after the coordinator's GREENLIGHT.
## Decisions (owner, 2026-11-21)
- the release SHA-1, supplied by the owner;
- the debug SHA-1 of this machine's debug keystore, which signs the emulator builds.
-**Still open** (the coordinator will ask the owner):
-- which Google account is used on the emulator;
-- the same Cloud project as desktop or a new one;
-- the publishing setup: Personal mode, In production unverified, or Testing.

+5. **Emulator account:** a throwaway Google account holding only synthetic mail. The owner signs it into the emulator through the Device panel when stage 7 needs it. At that point B stops with `BLOCKED:` and the exact steps.
+6. **Publishing: External, Testing, with weekly re-consent.** The owner chose this over Personal mode.
+7. **One project: the existing desktop Google Cloud project** (coordinator's decision, fewer steps). It holds:
+   - both Android clients: the release SHA-1 and this VM's debug SHA-1;
+   - the owner's account and the throwaway account as test users.
+8. **The weekly expiry must be clean.** When the grant expires, the app shows **Sign-in expired** with **Sign in again**. Nothing is lost:
+   - the cache, drafts, reminders and local state stay;
+   - queued writes stay queued;
+   - after re-consent for the same account, queued writes resume and mailbox actions stay enabled.
+   A test that an expired grant produces this state replaces the earlier 8-day "lasting sign-in" check (section 1, Validation plan).
## Context

The Android build is a fixture-only app. One person should be able to use it with their own Gmail account. This ADR decides how the phone signs in, where it keeps credentials, how the user moves between the demo mailbox and Gmail, and what runs when.

**How the emulator gets a registered signer:** stage 3 onward installs only debug APKs built on this VM, which are signed by the registered debug key. CI debug artifacts are never used for sign-in tests.
- If `~/.android/debug.keystore` is deleted or regenerated, its SHA-1 changes and the debug client must be registered again. The stage 7 report records the SHA-1 used.

-  - Google is expected to refuse registering the same package + SHA-1 pair in two clients, across projects too (to confirm at registration). The debug client therefore lives in the project whose account signs in on the emulator, and the release client in the project the owner uses daily. Those can be the same project or two projects (still open).

+  - Google is expected to refuse registering the same package + SHA-1 pair in two clients, across projects too (to confirm at registration). The debug client therefore lives in the project whose account signs in on the emulator, and the release client in the project the owner uses daily. Both are in the existing desktop project (Decision 7).
- A release APK is not debuggable, so `run-as` checks run only on the emulator's debug build.

- **No client id in the build.** Play services matches package + signature. "Configured" therefore cannot be known before the first call. A `DEVELOPER_ERROR` result (package/SHA-1 not registered) maps to `not_configured`, with a next step that says this build is not registered. "Play services missing or too old" maps to `unsupported_platform` on connect. The account status says so plainly; it is not shown as an expired sign-in.

- **Bridge:** a Kotlin class in the Android app (`GoogleAuthBridge`), registered as an Android plugin from Rust with `tauri::plugin::Builder` and `register_android_plugin`. Rust calls it with `PluginHandle::run_mobile_plugin` from worker threads, never from the main thread. **The webview cannot call it:** no plugin permission is added to `main-window`, and tokens never cross IPC. Operations:
- `LoopbackPkceSource` is today's code, unchanged in behaviour, used on desktop.

- `PlatformAuthorizerSource` sits over a small `PlatformAuthorizer` trait (`authorize`, `clear_token`). On Android its implementation is the bridge. In tests it is a scripted fake, so the whole Android path is tested on Linux.

- **Token lifetime on Android:** the access token lives only in process memory with its expiry. Before expiry, and after a 401, the source clears the cached token (`clearToken`) and calls `authorize(interactive = false)` **once**. A second failure is `AuthRequired`. No refresh token exists on the phone.

+- **Weekly expiry in Testing** (Decision 8). When a test user's grant expires, the silent `authorize` returns `needsUserInteraction`, which becomes `AuthRequired`. Today's code already gives this the right outcome:
+  - The connection becomes `auth_required`, shown as **Sign-in expired** with **Sign in again**.
+  - The worker treats `AuthRequired` as account-wide: the write is requeued, not failed (`crates/mail-core/src/gmail/operations.rs:91-103`), and the pass stops.
+  - Cached reading, drafts, reminders, the saved split and Undo history stay.
+  - Search falls back to cached results with its disclosure (`gmail/sync.rs:680-695`).

+  **Sign in again** runs Connect for the bound account (pinned with `setAccount`), asking for the stored scopes. If modify was granted, it is asked for again, so mailbox actions stay enabled after re-consent. Afterwards the queued writes run in their original order. Nothing in this path clears the binding or the cache; only **Disconnect** does. Stages 2 and 6 test this.
### 2. Token storage on Android

- `AndroidKeystoreSecrets` implements `Secrets`. It stores the serialized `TokenBundle` encrypted with an AES-256-GCM Keystore key (alias `email-os-gmail-binding`, no user authentication required, so sync can run while the app is open and unlocked). The file is in `noBackupFilesDir`. Under option C the bundle holds **no token material**: only the account id, the address and the granted scopes (section 4). The token fields stay in the type for desktop. On Android they are always empty, and a test asserts the stored JSON has no token.

| **External, In production, not verified** | The app "might display an 'unverified app' screen before it displays the consent screen" ([Unverified apps](https://support.google.com/cloud/answer/7454865)). It is limited to "100 new users in total", over the project's lifetime ([Manage app audience](https://support.google.com/cloud/answer/15549945)). The restricted-scope verification page names personal use as a case where verification may not be needed: "if you are the only user of your app or if your app is used by only a few users, all of whom are known personally to you" ([Restricted scope verification](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2/production-readiness/restricted-scope-verification)). Google states the 7-day expiry **only** for Testing. It does **not** say whether authorizations last longer for an unverified production app with restricted scopes. The general expiry rules (six months unused; password change for Gmail scopes) still apply. | The owner clicks through the unverified-app screen at each consent. That expected screen is the only ongoing cost. **Unconfirmed:** whether consent survives past 7 days. To check, at least 8 days after consent, kill and relaunch the app; it must sync with no sign-in UI (validation plan). |

| **Personal mode** (user type chosen when the project is created) | "Personal mode apps do not require OAuth app verification, are not subject to the OAuth user cap or 7-day test user token expiration, and do not display the unverified app screen." "Only the Google Account that created the Personal mode application can sign in or authorize scopes for its OAuth clients." It is "a one-time selection when configuring a new application": an existing project cannot switch. Android is listed as a client type ([Manage app audience](https://support.google.com/cloud/answer/15549945); [Personal mode onboarding](https://support.google.com/cloud/answer/15544987#personal-mode-onboarding)). These pages do not list scope restrictions, and they do not say explicitly that restricted Gmail scopes are allowed. Workspace accounts "might still require configuration by your organization's administrators". | Fits a one-person app exactly: no weekly expiry, no unverified screen, no cap. It needs a **new** project, created **by the account whose mail the phone reads**. **To check at setup:** **Data access** accepts the Gmail scopes, and the first Connect shows no unverified-app screen. |

-**Recommendation:** **Personal mode**, in a new project created by the Google account the owner will read on the phone. If it does not accept the Gmail scopes, or is not offered for that account, use **External, In production, not verified**. Keep the "unverified app" screen at consent, and confirm the 8-day check before relying on it. **Testing** is only for a throwaway validation account. Because a Personal project accepts only its creator, a throwaway emulator account needs its own small project: either its own Personal project created while signed in as that account, or an External Testing project where it is a test user.

+**Decided (2026-11-21):** **External, Testing**, in the existing desktop project, with weekly re-consent (Decisions 6–7). The table above is kept as the record of the alternatives. The app must handle the weekly expiry cleanly (Decision 8, section 1).
### Steps

-1. **Create the project.** For Personal mode, open the Personal mode onboarding (Google Cloud console → Google Auth Platform → Overview → personal onboarding, `console.cloud.google.com/auth/overview/personal`) while signed in as the account the phone will read. Otherwise use an External project. Enable **Gmail API** under **APIs & Services → Library**.
+1. **Use the existing desktop project.** Confirm **Gmail API** is enabled under **APIs & Services → Library**.
2. **Google Auth Platform → Branding:** app name, user support email, developer contact. No logo is needed.
-3. **Google Auth Platform → Audience** (External projects only):
-   - For daily use, set **Publish app** to **In production**, with no verification submission.
-   - For a throwaway validation project, keep **Testing** and add the throwaway account as a **Test user**.

+3. **Google Auth Platform → Audience:** user type **External**, publishing status **Testing**. Under **Test users**, add the owner's Google account and the throwaway emulator account. Do not publish, and do not submit for verification.

4. **Google Auth Platform → Data access:** add `.../auth/gmail.readonly` and `.../auth/gmail.modify`. Track D adds `.../auth/gmail.send` only for accounts without modify. Do not submit for verification.
5. **Google Auth Platform → Clients → Create client → Android:**
- Package name: `dev.exedev.emailos` (Decision 4) for both clients.

-   - **Release client:** the SHA-1 of the owner's release certificate. ADR 0004's owner steps print it (`keytool -list -v -keystore <release.jks> -alias <alias>`). Register it in the project the owner uses daily.
-   - **Debug client:** `93:06:D5:83:0B:27:BE:95:BB:48:80:7B:52:9C:95:D5:C8:18:C6:03`, this VM's debug key. Register it in the project whose account signs in on the emulator.
+   - **Release client:** the SHA-1 of the owner's release certificate. ADR 0004's owner steps print it (`keytool -list -v -keystore <release.jks> -alias <alias>`).
+   Both go in the existing desktop project.

Leave **Advanced settings → custom URI scheme** off. No Web client, no secret. No client id has to be sent to me or put in the build. If Google refuses a pair as "already in use", it is registered in another client; delete it there first.

-6. **For the emulator run:** sign a throwaway Google account into the emulator yourself through the T3 Device panel (**Settings → Passwords & accounts**, or the account chooser during Connect). I never type, see or store the password. Put a few synthetic messages in that account so the recording contains no real mail. With an account signed in, the emulator's Play Store can update Google Play services if stage 3 finds the installed version too old.

+6. **For the emulator run** (when B reports `BLOCKED:` at stage 7): sign the throwaway Google account into the emulator yourself through the T3 Device panel (**Settings → Passwords & accounts**, or the account chooser during Connect). I never type, see or store the password. Put a few synthetic messages in that account so the recording contains no real mail. With an account signed in, the emulator's Play Store can update Google Play services if stage 3 finds the installed version too old.
7. **For your phone** (after track A's install path works): confirm it has Google Play services, install the APK signed with a registered key, and run the short checklist in the Validation plan.
8. **Verification and the security assessment** for public distribution are **not** needed and are not requested here.
- a covered request (for example `Readonly` with modify stored) returns `AlreadyCovered` and the fake authorizer records zero calls.
Existing `gmail::provider` tests are unchanged and pass.

-2. **Credential seam.** Extract `CredentialSource` from `LiveGmailProvider`: `access_token`, `authorize(scopes, account, interactive)`, `invalidate(token)`. `LoopbackPkceSource` wraps today's `auth.rs`, with identical behaviour. Add `PlatformAuthorizerSource` over the `PlatformAuthorizer` trait and a scripted fake covering granted, missing modify, cancelled, needs-interaction, developer error, Play services missing, wrong account, network, and 401 → one silent retry → `AuthRequired`. *Check:* all existing provider and auth tests pass untouched; the new fake-driven tests pass; `cargo clippy` is clean.

+2. **Credential seam.** Extract `CredentialSource` from `LiveGmailProvider`: `access_token`, `authorize(scopes, account, interactive)`, `invalidate(token)`. `LoopbackPkceSource` wraps today's `auth.rs`, with identical behaviour. Add `PlatformAuthorizerSource` over the `PlatformAuthorizer` trait and a scripted fake covering granted, missing modify, cancelled, needs-interaction, developer error, Play services missing, wrong account, network, and 401 → one silent retry → `AuthRequired`. It also covers the **weekly-expiry** case: a bound account with modify and a queued write, then a silent `authorize` that returns `needsUserInteraction`. The test asserts:
+   - the status is `auth_required`;
+   - the write is still queued, not failed;
+   - the cache and drafts are intact;

+   - after an interactive `authorize` for the same account, the stored scopes still include modify and the queued write is applied once. *Check:* all existing provider and auth tests pass untouched; the new fake-driven tests pass; `cargo clippy` is clean.
3. **Android bridge and Keystore secrets** (after track A is merged; based on A's package path and manifest). Add the Kotlin `GoogleAuthBridge`:
- Authorization API, with the `PendingIntent` launched through `MainActivity`;
- `clearToken`, reporting `unsupported` when the device's Play services lacks it;
- **Disconnect** → **Not connected**, cache gone, drafts kept, Keystore file gone (`run-as` listing only; file contents are never printed).

- A screen recording (≤60 s) of Connect through first sync. It contains the account address and mail, so it is **not committed**. It is kept in `/home/exedev/email-os-usable/android-gmail/` and listed in the PR, unless the account holds only synthetic mail and the owner agrees to commit it.
- On the owner's phone (after track A): install, Connect, sync, Enable mailbox actions, archive + Undo, background/resume. The owner reports the results; no screenshots of real mail are committed.

-- **Lasting sign-in:** at least 8 days after the owner's first consent on the phone, in the project set up for daily use (Personal mode, or In production unverified), kill and relaunch the app. It must sync with no sign-in UI. This is the check for what Google does not document (Owner actions). The owner reports the result.

+- **Weekly expiry, on the emulator:** with a write queued (archive while in airplane mode), remove the app's access in the throwaway account's Google settings to stand in for the 7-day expiry, then restore the network. The app must show **Sign-in expired** → **Sign in again**, with the cached inbox and the draft still there and the archive still pending. After re-consent the archive is applied and mailbox actions are still enabled. Screenshots of each step use the synthetic-mail account.
## Risks and open questions

- Inferred, not documented: `authorize()` predates the 21.x library releases, so 24.23.35 very likely supports it. Then the emulator can run the real flow with a throwaway Google account. `clearToken` may be missing from a June 2024 Play services (B does not use `revokeAccess`).

- Handling: stage 3's probe records what the emulator supports. The bridge treats a missing `clearToken` as `unsupported` and degrades as described in section 1. With a throwaway account signed in, the Play Store can update Play services; an update changes the emulator, so it needs the coordinator's agreement. The owner's phone, with current Play services, is the final check either way.

- **Bridge mechanics.** A blocking `run_mobile_plugin` call that waits on an activity result must not deadlock with the main thread, and the `PendingIntent` result must reach the bridge after a configuration change. Stage 3 proves this before anything depends on it.

-- **Consent lifetime.** Testing expires every 7 days (documented). Personal mode documents no 7-day expiry, but its pages do not say explicitly that restricted Gmail scopes are allowed. Unverified production has no documented 7-day rule but no positive statement either. The 8-day check in the validation plan settles it for the chosen setup.

+- **Consent lifetime.** Testing expires every 7 days (documented), so the owner re-consents weekly by choice (Decision 6). The risk is a messy expiry path, not the expiry itself. It is covered by the stage 2 test and the emulator check above.
- **Process freeze in background.** Android may freeze or kill the process during a write. This relies on the existing outcome-unknown reconciliation; no new guarantee is claimed.
- **Package rename by track A** after the Android client is registered means a new client. Register only after A's rename is merged.
**Open questions for the owner**
-Questions 1–3 were decided on 2026-11-21 (see Decisions), and 4–5 were resolved by the coordinator. Still open:

-6. Which **Google account** will be used on the emulator? A throwaway one is recommended, holding only synthetic mail. Will you sign it in yourself through the Device panel when stage 7 starts? This also decides which project holds the debug client.

-7. **Same Cloud project as desktop, or a new one?** A Personal mode project must be new, because existing projects cannot switch to Personal. Desktop can keep its current project, or add a Desktop client in the new one later.
-8. **Publishing setup for daily use:** Personal mode (recommended), In production without verification, or Testing with weekly re-consent? See Owner actions.
+None. Questions 1–3 and 6–8 were decided on 2026-11-21 (Decisions 1–7), and 4–5 were resolved by the coordinator.
